about: Money patterns Verse copies, each from a documented real business, each with the source that was read. The revenue lane (tools/revenue-lane.mjs) only tests copy built from these; every finished experiment adds its result here, and the pattern's score decides how often it is tried next. docs/money-playbook.md.

patterns.what: Keep the product free and name, plainly, what the paid plan adds on top.
patterns.proof: Read the Docs: a free community service plus a paid Business plan; donations alone did not work for them. Photopea: free editor, paid Premium alongside.

patterns.what: Put one quiet offer on the pages that already get the most time, instead of waiting for people to find the store.
patterns.proof: Photopea earns from the hours people already spend in the editor; Read the Docs runs a single non-tracking ad on the docs readers already read.

patterns.what: Send the button straight to the payment form, one step fewer.
patterns.proof: Gumroad documents ?wanted=true for opening the payment form directly from a creator's own site.

patterns.what: Lead with the free week when checkout really has one, and say the reminder and cancel terms out loud.
patterns.proof: Plausible grew to $1M ARR with no popups or dark patterns, cancel any time, and a reminder before renewals.
patterns.template: Try {name} {trial}: {blurb_lc}. You get an email before it renews at {price_bare}, and you can cancel any time.

patterns.what: Sell the tool builders already use here, priced small and per month or per call.
patterns.proof: x402 is an open standard for charging per API request over HTTP, for people and agents, with no accounts; Verse already sells calls that way.
